# JTTY (from WSJT-X)

JTTY is a digital text mode introduced in WSJT-X 3.3 (BETA 1 at the time of
the port): non-slotted 4-GFSK at 31.25 baud, a 13-symbol sync sequence plus 46
coded symbols per 1.888 s frame, and a tail-biting K=10 rate-1/2 convolutional
code with a 12-bit CRC. PiRO transmits and receives it in pure JavaScript, with no
WSJT-X binaries involved.

| | |
|---|---|
| Upstream | WSJT-X, `release/3.3` branch (commit `57ba933`), https://github.com/WSJTX/wsjtx |
| Upstream licence | GNU GPL version 3 (`COPYING` in the WSJT-X tree) |
| PiRO licence | AGPL-3.0-only (GPL-3.0 section 13 permits combining the two) |

## What was ported

| PiRO file | WSJT-X source |
|---|---|
| `src/audio/jtty-codec.js` | `lib/jtty/jtty_source_codec.f90` (atoms, packing, unpacking, rendering), `lib/jtty/jtty_mod.f90` (`pack_jtty`, the minimum-frame dynamic program, text normalization), the standard-callsign parts of `lib/77bit/packjt77.f90` (`pack28`, `unpack28`, `chkcall`, `callok`) and `lib/77bit/packjt77_grammar.f90` (ARRL section table, callsign shape) |
| `src/audio/jtty-rx.js` | `lib/jtty/jtty_mdecode.f90` and its helpers: analytic signal, sync surface and candidate search, `jtty_peakup`, payload correlation, the three-channel search (main band plus 1350 / 1650 Hz), subtraction and second pass, and message assembly (duplicates, continuation, gap marker, expiry); SNR estimate |
| `src/audio/jtty-tbcc-decode.js` | the tail-biting list-WAVA decoder (`tbcc.f90`, `jtty_tbcc_code_profile.f90`): width 4, 2 wraps, 4 hypotheses, the L=1,2,4 coherent ladder plus half-symbol L=1, CRC-12 check |
| `src/audio/decimator.js`, `jtty-decode-worker.js`, `src/server/jtty-decoder-bridge.js` | PiRO's own glue: streaming 48 kHz to 12 kHz decimation, a worker thread, and a load governor that drops to a lighter search on a slow machine |
| `src/audio/jtty-tx.js` | `lib/jtty/tbcc.f90` (`tbcc_encode`, `encode_crc12`), `lib/jtty/jtty_tbcc_code_profile.f90`, `lib/jtty/jtty_fec_mod.f90` (sync sequence), `lib/jtty/genjtty.f90`, `lib/jtty/gen_jttywave.f90`, `lib/gfsk_pulse.f90` |

The canonical specification is `lib/jtty/jtty_source_encoding.txt` in the
WSJT-X tree. Everything the wire format defines is implemented for
transmission: all call actions, all STRUCT30 families (serial, location,
pair, serial+time, control phrases, grid), TEXT5, and the Unknown / Field Day
/ RTTY Roundup exchange profiles. PiRO's Send button uses the Unknown profile
(plain text).

Not ported: the retrospective re-sweeps of earlier windows, the N1MM
tagged-text interface and the native function-key macros (the last two belong
to WSJT-X's GUI layer, not to the mode itself). The receiver searches one
configurable audio range (by default the whole 200-2900 Hz passband) plus
the two fixed channels.

## How the port is checked

`test/jtty.test.js` compares the port against the WSJT-X reference encoder:

* the ten representative 34-bit vectors printed in the specification;
* `test/fixtures/jtty-vectors.json`: 401 messages (all three exchange
  profiles, one to sixteen frames) whose frame counts, canonical text and
  complete channel-symbol sequences were generated by WSJT-X's own `sjtty`
  program, built from the sources above. Every one must match exactly;
* `test/fixtures/jtty-cq-k1abc-cq-1500hz.i16`: one frame of reference audio
  from `sjtty`. The port matches it to a relative RMS error of about 3e-4 (the
  reference accumulates phase in single precision and reads a 65 536-entry
  sine table).

`test/jtty-rx.test.js` checks the receiver. The port was compared with
WSJT-X's own decoder (`rjtty`, built from the same sources) on twenty
generated recordings and on the official sample `samples/JTTY/260807_134110.wav`
(kept as `test/fixtures/jtty-wsjtx-sample-260807_134110.wav`): decoded text,
frequency and sync agreed on every file. Further tests cover clean and noisy
signals, two simultaneous signals, lost frames, chunk-size invariance and the
receive bridge. In normal mode the sample also yields one spurious
false decode that WSJT-X's decoder produces too.

See `test/fixtures/README-jtty.md` for how the fixtures were made and how to
regenerate them.

## Caveats

JTTY is a beta mode and the frame format carries no version field. If a later
WSJT-X release changes the format, this port will silently stop being
compatible until it is updated and the fixtures regenerated.
